# The engine e2e tier's shards run past the five-minute step ceiling

## Context

On dev's push of `e161f623bf` (2026-10-17 21:02Z), two of the three `e2e-engine` shards failed while every test passed. Shard 1 reported `133 passed (5.1m)` and shard 3 `87 passed (5.1m)`, and both ended with `##[error]The action 'Run e2e (engine tier)' has timed out after 5 minutes.` On #19842, shard 1 fails the same way. The `✘` lines in those logs belong to `WorkerErrorGate.spec.mjs`'s `test.fail()` twins and are expected.

## The Problem

The tier has grown into its ceiling. Every engine-touching PR, and dev itself, now goes red on time alone, so a real failure in this check can no longer be told from the clock. That matters right before the 13.3 cut (#19652).

## The Architectural Reality

`.github/workflows/test-e2e.yml` runs the tier as a matrix of 3 shards (`shard: [1, 2, 3]`, `shards: [3]`), and the `Run e2e (engine tier)` step has `timeout-minutes: 5` outside `workflow_dispatch`.

Design authority, from the workflow's header: "the ceiling is five minutes of test time per shard, enforced on the step below … A shard nearing it gets a sibling, never a higher ceiling: the ceiling is the wait every pull request pays." The same rule already moved the tier from 1 to 2 shards (#18896) and from 2 to 3 (#19079).

## The Fix

Run four shards: `shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]`, `shards: [4]`. The ceiling, the dispatch path and the selection in `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs` stay as they are.

**The merge gate becomes one stable context** (added 2026-10-17 after Emmy's CI hold on #19844). Dev's ruleset `19087298` requires `e2e-engine (1/3)`, `(2/3)` and `(3/3)` by name. A shard's name carries the shard count, so four shards report contexts the ruleset never asks for, and every pull request would block. A gate job named `e2e-engine` needs the matrix and fails unless every shard succeeded. The ruleset then requires that one name, and the next sibling shard needs no ruleset edit. The swap is the operator's: in ruleset `19087298`, replace the three shard contexts with `e2e-engine` and keep every other required context and field.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The engine tier runs as four shards on pull requests and dev pushes; `workflow_dispatch` still runs one. Shown by PR run 39074515285 and dev push run 39083652076 at the merge `e0704c93bb`, each with `e2e-engine (1/4)` … `(4/4)`.
- [x] On the fix PR's own run, every shard's test step finishes under five minutes, with each shard's time recorded in the PR: 218 / 116 / 139 / 186 s (#19844 comment 6241630206).
- [x] An `e2e-engine` context reports on the fix PR's head, succeeds when every shard succeeds, and fails if any shard does not. It reported success at `35eb58f821` (22:23:35 → 22:23:38 UTC). The failure path holds by construction (`test "${SHARDS}" = success` on the matrix result); no failing run has exercised it yet.
- [x] *(operator, at merge)* Ruleset `19087298` requires `e2e-engine` in place of the three shard contexts. The operator made the swap 2026-10-18. A live read of `rules/branches/dev` at 00:23Z shows `e2e-engine` (integration 15368) with no shard context, and every other required context unchanged.
- [x] *(post-merge)* dev's next push reports the engine tier green. Open PRs pick up the gate on their next dev merge. Run 39083652076 at `e0704c93bb` succeeded: four shards, each between 3m23s and 4m33s, then the `e2e-engine` gate at 00:45:49 → 00:45:53 UTC.

## Out of Scope

- The ceiling itself, which the header rules out.
- Rebalancing by test weight (`PWTEST_SHARD_WEIGHTS`).
- The Brain-gated tier (#19655).
